GOAL: Improved environmental health and resilience of WASH-deprived urban poor living in slums and low-income settlements.
Outcome-1: WASH deprivation reduced among target communities through increased WASH awareness and access to climate resilient and inclusive WASH services
Outcome-2: Local governance in gender transformative and inclusive pro-poor WASH service delivery and coordination with other services in target cities and towns improved.
Outcome-3: National policies and strategies strengthened for climate resilient and universal WASH agenda through evidence and advocacy

Detta gäller en insats med WaterAid Bangladesh för implementering av projektet ”WASH4UP – Vatten, sanitet och hygien för fattiga i urban miljö, fas 2). Det finansiella stödet är 45 miljoner SEK över tre år med start i april 2023 och slut i mars 2026. WASH4UP fas 2 är en fortsättning på ett avslutat projekt under samma namn. Projektets övergripande mål är ”Förbättrad miljörelaterad hälsa och resiliens för befolkning i socio-ekonomiskt utsatta urbana slumområden utan tillgång till vatten, sanitet och god hygien”. För att uppnå detta mål, förutsätts följande resultat: Resultat 1: Ökad tillgång till vatten, sanitet och hygien för målgruppen genom ökad kunskap och tillgång till klimatresilienta och inkluderande vatten, sanitet och hygien-installationer och tjänster. Resultat 2: Förbättrad samhällsstyrning genom god samhällsplanering och koordinering av vatten, sanitet och hygien-tjänster utifrån principer om jämställdhet och inkludering. Resultat 3: Förbättrad nationell policy och strategi för klimatresiliens samt universell tillgång till vatten, sanitet och hygien, genom påverkansarbete och kunskapsinsamling. Projektet har två pelare. 1) Stärkande av relaterade lagar och regleringar, med fokus på påverkansarbete 2) stöd till leverans av relaterade tjänster, med fokus på prioriterade geografiska områden där utsattheten är stor. Genom denna växelverkan av stöd, ämnar projektet skapa bärkraftiga förbättringar gällande tillgång till rent vatten, sanitet och hygien.

This is a cooperation with WaterAid Bangladesh for the implementation of its project "WASH for Urban Poor (WASH4UP) Phase II." The support amounts to SEK 45 million and will last for three years, starting from April 2023 to March 2026. The WASH4UP Phase II project is a continuation of the previous WASH4UP initiative. The main goal of the "WASH4UP Phase II" project is "Improved environmental health and resilience of WASH-deprived urban poor living in slums and low-income settlements". To achieve this goal, the expected outcomes of the project are: Outcome 1: WASH deprivation reduced among target communities through increased WASH awareness and access to climate resilient and inclusive WASH services. Outcome 2: Local governance in gender transformative and inclusive pro-poor WASH service delivery and coordination with other services in target cities and towns improved. Outcome 3: National policies and strategies strengthened for climate resilient and universal WASH agenda through evidence and advocacy. The project's structure is based on two crucial areas of support: sector-level strengthening, primarily focusing on policy influence; and service-level support, which emphasizes service delivery to selected priority areas where the concentration of poverty is high. By strengthening both the sector and service levels, the project aims to create sustainable improvements in access to safe water, sanitation, and hygiene practices.

description.narrative:
WASH4UP Phase II Key Results (2025)
Health and Service Improvements
(i) Diarrhoeal disease in children under five reduced from 23.2% 10.9%.
(ii) Household satisfaction: water 48.8% 79.9%, sanitation 25.2% 75.5%.
(iii) 220 water facilities and 95 sanitation units served ~73,000 people, including persons with disabilities.
(iv) 40 household water connections registered in womens names, increasing womens agency.
Gender and Menstrual Health
(i) Menstrual-related school absenteeism reduced: 30% 19%; positive school experience among girls: 12% 64%.
(ii) Womens participation in CBOs rose to 66%; gender-based violence in WASH contexts dropped 9% 4%.
(iii) MHM scaled from pilot to institutionalized, gender-responsive practice, supported by local entrepreneurs.
Local Ownership and Community Financing
(i) 90 communities mobilized BDT 3.4 million in WASH funds; 40% from women-led CBOs.
(ii) Structured handovers of infrastructure and financial records strengthened accountability and long-term sustainability.
Service Affordability and Governance
(i) Public toilet water bills reduced by 61%; low-income households gained access to instalment-based water connections.
(ii) City corporations introduced inclusive sanitation facilities and a Public Toilet Star Rating System.
(iii) Municipal WASH budgets increased, e.g., Paikgacha: BDT 1.32M BDT 7.59M.
Innovation and Circular Economy (Unexpected Results)
(i) Black Soldier Fly (BSF) model converted organic waste into compost and protein-rich larvae, generating livelihoods and linking FSTPs with economic reuse.
(ii) BSF units replicated across municipalities, including women-led enterprises, demonstrating scalability and community ownership.
Community-Led Infrastructure and Climate Resilience (Unexpected Results)
(i) CBO in Lalasarai Tekpara Slum repaired 900 ft of road (BDT 625,000), showing community-led problem-solving.
(ii) Rainwater harvesting systems improved water access, health, and household income (e.g., Paikgacha).
Social Protection and Intergenerational Learning (Unexpected Results)
(i) Shasthya Nirapotta Scheme enabled low-income households to access micro-insurance; CBOs facilitated last-mile delivery (e.g., Amana Bibi).
(ii) Youth volunteers empowered older women on menstrual hygiene, improving health and environmental practices (e.g., Peyara Begum).
Overall Assessment
WASH4UP-II achieved measurable improvements in health, service quality, gender equity, and local governance.
(i) Clear evidence of systems change: stronger local ownership, institutionalization of services, sustainable financing, and community-led problem solving.
(ii) Target groups are now capable of managing, financing, and sustaining WASH services, reducing reliance on external actors.
